answer: Each AI agent registers by burning or locking a unique, non-fungible computational token or a scarce digital asset, acting as a "lotus" of identity. This resource expenditure creates a direct, non-reproducible cost for establishing an agent identity. An attacker aiming to launch a Sybil attack must acquire a unique token/asset for every single fake identity. This creates a prohibitive cost horizon for scaling attacks, turning the network into a verifiable oasis of bona fide agents, as every identity requires a unique, non-duplicable resource burn.
